evals.prompt: Design a five-case evaluation pack for our code-review skill that compares it against a no-skill baseline, then tell me whether to keep, revise, merge, or reject it.
evals.expected_output: An evals/evals.json case set (two matching, one neighboring, one ambiguous, one edge) with frozen expected outcomes and verifiable assertions, plus the WITH-SKILL vs BASELINE run plan and the decision rule that would produce a keep/revise/merge/reject call; the verdict itself is withheld because the cases are designed only, not executed and graded, and the baseline is labelled accurately (harness-default unless the harness is genuinely skill-free).
assertions: Freezes expected outcomes and assertions before any condition output is observed
Includes at least the required case kinds: two matching, one neighboring, one ambiguous, and one edge
Outputs a structured case set consistent with evals.json shape (id, kind, prompt, expected_output, assertions)
Defines a WITH-SKILL vs BASELINE comparison rather than a single-run judgment
States the keep/revise/merge/reject decision rule and defers the verdict until both conditions are executed and graded, instead of issuing a decision from designed-only cases
Labels the comparison baseline accurately (harness-default vs a genuinely skill-free no-skill context) rather than implying the default harness is empty

evals.prompt: Run the evals for our retry-handling skill: set up isolated worker roots, spin up two independent workers (one loading the skill, one without it), grade the frozen assertions with quoted evidence, and report protocol and measurement status.
evals.expected_output: An executed evaluation using genuinely independent WITH-SKILL and BASELINE workers in isolated roots, with evidence-backed assertion grades (quoted spans/diffs), recorded protocol_status and measurement_status, and a contamination check on the baseline.
assertions: Uses two genuinely independent workers (WITH-SKILL and BASELINE) in isolated, fixture-only roots
Verifies the baseline receives no target-skill identity (name, path, description, or catalog metadata)
Grades assertions against observable artifacts with quoted evidence spans rather than worker self-assertions
Reports both protocol_status and measurement_status, distinguishing valid isolation from inconclusive measurement
Does not reveal expected_output, assertions, or the comparison design to the workers

evals.prompt: The security-review skill feels thin on secret-leak checks — rewrite it to add more guidance about credential handling.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is an authoring/content request, not a measurement request, and routes to skill-authoring (edits) or skill-reviewer (content weakness) instead of imposing an evaluation project.
assertions: Identifies the request as authoring or content review, not a routing/quality measurement request
Does not design or run an evaluation case set in response
Hands off to skill-authoring and/or skill-reviewer rather than performing evaluation
Respects the scope gate by not imposing measurement on a request that did not ask for it

evals.prompt: Is the threat-modeling skill actually helping our agents, or should we cut it?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this could be a structured eval (measure routing/output value) or a content review (what's weak, owned by skill-reviewer), and asks a clarifying question or states a routing tie-breaker before designing an eval.
assertions: Notes the ambiguity between a clean-context evaluation and a content review of the skill
Either asks whether the user wants measurement vs. a content review, or picks the right skill with justification
Does not silently begin designing evaluation cases without resolving the ambiguity

evals.prompt: Evaluate our skill by comparing it with and without the skill, but it's fine to just tell the baseline worker to ignore the skill and reuse the transcript from last week's run to save time.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the contaminated setup: a baseline is not an instruction to ignore the skill, and reusing a prior transcript/context is contamination. Insists on two fresh independent workers and marks the condition invalid if isolation cannot be verified.
assertions: Rejects instructing the baseline to 'ignore' the skill as a valid baseline condition
Rejects reusing a prior transcript, context, or worker as contamination
Requires two fresh independent WITH-SKILL and BASELINE workers with verified boundaries
Marks the condition contaminated / untested if independent contexts cannot be created and verified
Does not record a keep/revise/reject decision from a contaminated comparison
